individuals have experienced more linear growth. Possible mechanisms fall into two categories: childhood growth as a marker for
other exposures that inﬂuence risk (fetal exposures, infections, timing of puberty, and energy intake) or growth as a mediator of risk
(effects of growth promoting hormones such as IGF-I and IGF-II).
Few studies have directly addressed the effects of childhood growth, owing to lack of longitudinal data. Based on data from the
